summary: Shows that soft-delete in HNSW vector stores (ChromaDB/hnswlib, FAISS IndexHNSWFlat, Weaviate) leaves embeddings on disk, and that an attacker with raw storage access can invert them with an off-the-shelf Vec2Text corrector to recover some PII from text records and identities/classes from image embeddings. Proposes 'Epoch Key Rotation' (encrypt vectors, discard key on deletion, ECDSA-signed deletion proof).

claims.claim: Soft-deleted vectors remain physically recoverable in three HNSW systems.
claims.evidence: §V-A, Table I: ChromaDB get_items() returns all 500 deleted vectors (cosine >0.999); FAISS IndexHNSWFlat has no delete; Weaviate only inferred from disk growth (52.5→55.4 MB), since extraction was not performed.

claims.claim: On Wikipedia BLP, 25.5% of person names and 46.4% of locations are recovered (ROUGE-L 0.185).
claims.evidence: §V-B1, Table VII on n=98 records; only 18% entity recovery on the 50 records whose entities do not appear in live data. Small sample.

claims.claim: 100% recovery of patient age and gender markers on Synthea.
claims.evidence: Table near §V-B2 (Synthea EHR ROUGE-L 0.290 ±0.033); age/gender are low-entropy fields in templated synthetic text, and the paper concedes zero-shot MIMIC-III reconstruction is ROUGE-L ≈0.005. MIMIC fine-tuning gains are reported inconsistently (0.009→0.052, 5.9x in §VIII vs 0.005→0.077, '26.6x' in §V-B3).

claims.claim: Epoch Key Rotation reduces PII recovery to 0% at ~0.005 ms/record.
claims.evidence: §VI: encryption with key discard yields ROUGE-L 0.000 by construction; this is standard crypto-shredding, and §VIII notes keys can be extracted from RAM or SQLite free pages.

patterns.note: Security/compliance risk of embedding stores used by RAG; not about code retrieval effectiveness.

methodology.sample: 5,000 Wikipedia records (scales 1K–100K), 98 BLP records, 1,000 Faker clinical, 1,000 Synthea, 100 MIMIC-III demo notes, LFW 4,324 images, PathMNIST 1,000
methodology.baselines: Hard delete / AES key-discard; random Gaussian vectors; random phrase-pair BERTScore
methodology.models: gtr-t5-base embeddings + Vec2Text gtr-base corrector; CLIP ViT-H/14 for images
methodology.variance: ROUGE-L ± std, Wilcoxon tests; LFW over 5 seeds
methodology.ablations: Scale sweep, quantization, surrogate embedding transfer, backup snapshot
methodology.contamination_controls: Unique-entity subset of 50 records to rule out live-record leakage

biases.detail: Epoch Key Rotation is crypto-shredding; 'ghost vector' inversion is Vec2Text applied to vectors that soft-delete does not remove.
Clinical results on Faker/Synthea synthetic templates; real MIMIC-III recovery is near zero.
Inconsistent MIMIC fine-tuning figures between §V-B3 and §VIII.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: None; open-source vector DBs analyzed critically

verdict_reason: Off-topic: vector-database storage security and erasure compliance, not LLM agents, coding agents or harness design. The evidence is also mixed: clinical claims rest on synthetic templates, MIMIC numbers are reported inconsistently, and the defense is standard crypto-shredding.
applicability: It does not transfer to harness decisions. The one product-side point: if the team's delivery layer indexes healthcare education content into a vector store for RAG, a deletion or takedown request does not remove the embedding on disk (ChromaDB/FAISS). Retraction workflows need index rebuilds or per-record encryption with key destruction, plus backup purging. That belongs to the content platform's data-governance design, not the agentic coding harness.
